module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 10

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/10](https://www.erdosproblems.com/10)
- [Cr71] Crocker, R., On the sum of a prime and of two powers of two. Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971),
  103-107.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos10

/--
The set of natural numbers that can be written as a sum
of a prime and at most $k$ powers of $2$.
-/
abbrev sumPrimeAndTwoPows (k : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  { p + (pows.map (2 ^ ·)).sum | (p : ℕ) (pows : Multiset ℕ) (_ : p.Prime)
    (_ : pows.card ≤ k)}

/--
Is there some $k$ such that every integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ k, sumPrimeAndTwoPows k = Set.univ \ {0, 1} := by
  sorry

/--
Gallagher [Ga75] has shown that for any $ϵ > 0$ there exists $k(ϵ)$
such that the set of integers which are the sum of a prime and at most $k(ϵ)$
many powers of $2$ has lower density at least $1 - ϵ$.

Ref: Gallagher, P. X., _Primes and powers of 2_.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.gallagher (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ k, 1 - ε ≤ (sumPrimeAndTwoPows k).lowerDensity := by
  sorry

/--
Granville and Soundararajan [GrSo98] have conjectured that at most $3$
powers of $2$ suffice for all odd integers, and hence at most $4$ powers of $2$
suffice for all even integers.

Ref: Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., _A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$_
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.granville_soundararajan_odd :
    {n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ 1 < n} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 ∧
      {n : ℕ | Even n ∧ n ≠ 0} ⊆ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 4 := by
  sorry

/--
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that `1117175146` is not the sum of a prime
and at most $3$ powers of $2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk_example :
    1117175146 ∉ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many even integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_10.variants.two_pows :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Bogdan Grechuk has observed that $1117175146$ is not the sum of a prime and at most $3$
powers of $2$, and pointed out that parity considerations, coupled with the fact that there
are many integers not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$ suggest that there exist
infinitely many even integers which are not the sum of a prime and at most $3$ powers of $2$.

This follows from Crocker's construction [Cr71] of infinitely many odd $t \equiv 15 \pmod{16}$
which are not the sum of a prime and $2$ powers of $2$: each such $t + 1$ is even and not the
sum of a prime and at most $3$ powers of $2$.

The linked Lean formalisation is by Daryxx, see comment section.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://gist.github.com/DaryxXx/e112c74cc648b08a420b0959315cf65f/4b347897ff1811f1db1d82594c581f54b8f31b7d#file-main-lean-L2287"]
theorem erdos_10.variants.grechuk :
    Set.Infinite <| {n : ℕ | Even n} \ sumPrimeAndTwoPows 3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos10

reformulations.difference: Lean asks for a uniform bound covering every natural number ≥ 2. Gallagher's concluding open problem (a), p. 141, asks about sufficiently large odd integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A uniform bound for sufficiently large odd integers extends to all odd integers > 1 by increasing the bound to cover finitely many exceptions. Every n ≥ 2 has some representation, for example 2 plus n−2 copies of 2^0. Each even n ≥ 4 is obtained from the odd integer n−1 by adding one further 2^0; 2 itself is prime. Conversely, the Lean condition immediately covers sufficiently large odd integers. This equivalence was proved as Review.main_iff_eventually_odd in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean qualitative density approximation concerns all natural numbers, whereas Gallagher introduces the result using relative density among odd integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If S_k covers a proportion at least 1−ε of odd integers in lower density, S_(k+1) also covers their even successors and contains S_k, giving lower density at least 1−ε among all integers. Conversely, an all-integer exceptional upper density δ gives an odd-relative exceptional upper density at most 2δ. Thus the ε-quantified qualitative assertions are equivalent. Exact versus at-most summand conventions do not change this qualitative conclusion: normalize zero exponents in odd representations, then split positive powers to obtain the desired number of terms; representations with too small a total power-sum lie in finitely many translates of the primes, a density-zero set.

reformulations.difference: Lean conjoins the source's odd-integer conjecture with the four-power assertion for positive even integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source explicitly conjectures that all odd integers > 1 are a prime plus at most three powers of two. For even n ≥ 4, represent n−1 and append 2^0. The remaining even case n=2 uses the prime 2 and the empty multiset. Hence the added conjunct follows from the first, and the conjunction is equivalent to the source conjecture. This equivalence was proved in scratch.lean.

could_not_verify: Erdos10.erdos_10.variants.grechuk_example: the numerical assertion was independently exhaustively verified, but Grechuk's original observation and attribution could not be compared directly with the inaccessible problem page/forum.
review.notes: No mathematical defect was found in the seven declarations. Boundary checks establish that 0 and 1 are never representable, every prime is representable with an empty multiset, and k=0 gives exactly the primes. The lower-density definition is the usual real-valued natural lower density, with finite counting intervals. A proved-equivalent Lean search and an independent exhaustive Python check both confirm the numerical counterexample for at most three powers. The linked infinitude proof was compiled after one non-mathematical tactic adjustment; its target depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The community database still records problem 10 as open. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/10 and its forum was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so current forum remarks and variant-status updates could not be checked directly. All experiments are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file is unchanged.
